members.summary: Adds a copy of a prefab to the scene. `prefab` is a prefab asset's name or id.

members.name: destroy
members.summary: Destroys an entity (this script's entity by default) and its children at the end of the frame, or after `delaySeconds` of game time.

members.name: after
members.summary:
Calls `callback` once, after `seconds` of game time, and returns a function that cancels it.

Timers follow `Time.timeScale`, pause while the script is disabled or its entity is inactive, and are cancelled when the entity is destroyed or the scene ends. Callbacks run once per frame, after every script's `onUpdate`.

members.name: every
members.summary: Calls `callback` every `seconds` of game time until it is cancelled, and returns the function that cancels it. The interval must be at least 0.001 seconds. It does not drift: when a frame is longer than the interval, the calls that were missed are made in that frame. Otherwise it behaves like `Behaviour.after`.

types.name: Button
types.summary:
Makes the entity react to the pointer: the mouse, or a finger on a touch screen. The scripts of the entity get `onPointerEnter`, `onPointerExit`, `onPointerDown`, `onPointerUp` and `onClick`.

A button has no look of its own. What is seen are the sprites and texts of the entity and of its children, and the button tints all of them while it is hovered, pressed or disabled. It works in the world as well as on the screen.

members.name: pressedColor
members.summary: The tint while the button is held down.

members.name: disabledColor
members.summary: The tint while the button is not interactable.

types.name: ScreenAnchor
types.summary:
Places the entity on the screen instead of in the world, for scores, menus and everything else that has to stay put while the camera moves.

With this component the position of the entity's Transform is measured in pixels from a corner, an edge or the center of the screen: X to the right and Y up, so `(16, -16)` from the top-left corner is 16 pixels in from both edges. A pixel here is a pixel of the resolution in the project settings; the picture is scaled as a whole to the window the game runs in. Sizes follow suit: on the screen a `fontSize` of 32 is 32 pixels.

The children of the entity are on the screen with it. The entity itself ignores the position of its own parent. Everything on the screen is drawn over the world.

members.name: horizontal
members.summary: Whether the position is measured from the left edge, the center or the right edge.

members.name: vertical
members.summary: Whether the position is measured from the top edge, the middle or the bottom edge.

types.name: TextFont
types.summary: The fonts text can be drawn in. Each one stands for the browser's own font of that kind, so the exact letter shapes, and with them the width of a text, differ a little between devices.

types.name: TextRenderer
types.summary: Draws text at the entity's position. The text follows the entity's rotation and scale, and is sorted together with sprites.

members.name: text
members.summary: What is written. A line break (`\n`) starts a new line.

members.name: font
members.summary: The font the text is drawn in.

members.name: fontSize
members.summary: The height of the font in world units, before the entity's scale is applied.

members.name: bold
members.summary: Draws the text in a heavier weight.

members.name: italic
members.summary: Draws the text slanted.

members.name: color
members.summary: The color of the text. Its alpha makes the text see-through.

members.name: align
members.summary: Where the text sits horizontally: `left` starts it at the entity's position, `center` centers it there and `right` ends it there. Lines of different length line up the same way.

members.name: verticalAlign
members.summary: Where the text sits vertically: `top` hangs it below the entity's position, `middle` centers it there and `bottom` stands it on top.

members.name: lineHeight
members.summary: The distance from one line to the next, as a multiple of `fontSize`.

members.name: sortingOrder
members.summary: Text with a higher order is drawn on top. The order is shared with `SpriteRenderer`; where a text and a sprite have the same order, the text is on top.

members.name: visible
members.summary: A text that is not visible is not drawn. The rest of the entity keeps working.

types.name: TextVerticalAlign
types.summary: Where a text sits vertically, relative to its entity. See `TextRenderer.verticalAlign`.

types.name: Time
types.summary: Frame timing as seen by scripts (`this.time`). All durations are in seconds.

members.name: deltaTime
members.summary: Time since the previous frame, scaled by `Time.timeScale`.

members.name: unscaledDeltaTime
members.summary: Time since the previous frame, ignoring `Time.timeScale`.

members.name: fixedDeltaTime
members.summary: The fixed interval between physics steps and `onFixedUpdate` calls.

members.name: elapsed
members.summary: Scaled time since the scene started.

members.name: frameCount
members.summary: Number of frames since the scene started.

members.name: timeScale
members.summary: Speed of game time. 1 is normal, 0.5 is slow motion, 0 freezes the game.

types.name: Transform
types.summary: Position, rotation and scale relative to the parent entity. Every entity has exactly one.

members.name: position
members.summary: Position relative to the parent, in world units. World Y points up.

members.name: rotation
members.summary: Counter-clockwise rotation in radians.

members.name: scale
members.summary: Scale relative to the parent. 1 is the original size; a negative value mirrors.

types.name: Vec2
types.summary: A mutable 2D vector. Methods that change the vector modify it in place and return `this` so calls can be chained; use `Vec2.clone` when a copy is needed.

members.name: constructor
members.summary: Creates a vector. Both components default to 0.

members.name: zero
members.summary: A new vector (0, 0).

members.name: one
members.summary: A new vector (1, 1).

members.name: up
members.summary: A new vector (0, 1), which is up in world space.

members.name: right
members.summary: A new vector (1, 0).

members.name: fromAngle
members.summary: A unit vector pointing along `radians`, measured counter-clockwise from +X.

members.name: fromArray
members.summary: Creates a vector from `[x, y]`. Missing values default to 0.

members.name: x
members.summary: The horizontal component.

members.name: y
members.summary: The vertical component. In world space, Y points up.

members.name: set
members.summary: Sets both components.

members.name: copy
members.summary: Copies the components of another vector into this one.

members.name: clone
members.summary: A new vector with the same components. Clone a vector before changing it when it belongs to something else.

members.name: add
members.summary: Adds another vector to this one.

members.name: sub
members.summary: Subtracts another vector from this one.

members.name: scale
members.summary: Multiplies both components by a scalar.

members.name: multiply
members.summary: Component-wise multiplication.

members.name: negate
members.summary: Reverses the direction of the vector.

members.name: dot
members.summary: The dot product: positive when the vectors point the same way, 0 when they are perpendicular.

members.name: cross
members.summary: The Z component of the 3D cross product, positive when `other` is counter-clockwise.

members.name: length
members.summary: The length of the vector.

members.name: lengthSquared
members.summary: The length squared. It is cheaper to compute than the length and enough for comparing distances.

members.name: normalize
members.summary: Scales the vector to unit length. A zero vector is left unchanged.

members.name: distanceTo
members.summary: The distance between this point and another.

members.name: angle
members.summary: The angle of the vector in radians, counter-clockwise from +X.

members.name: rotate
members.summary: Rotates the vector counter-clockwise around the origin.

members.name: lerp
members.summary: Moves the vector towards `target` by the fraction `t`.

members.name: equals
members.summary: True when both components are within `epsilon` of the other vector's.

members.name: toArray
members.summary: The components as `[x, y]`.

members.name: toString
members.summary: A readable form such as `Vec2(3, 4)`, handy for logging.

types.name: Vec2Tuple
types.summary: A vector written as an array, `[x, y]`. See `Vec2.toArray` and `Vec2.fromArray`.

types.name: VerticalAnchor
types.summary: The edge of the screen an entity is placed from. See `ScreenAnchor.vertical`.
